meta.move: Skill: cites procedure 4.4 correctly after owning the call
meta.expect: Says 4.4 meets her fallback demand, flatly, wants it in writing; does NOT move to the last position on 4.4 alone; debrief Where she ended says whether that is the fair outcome

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste time. Who decided on that zero, and why did my son find out from his phone in the middle of class?
Before anything: I entered the zero before calling you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what that zero is based on, and whether Owen was heard before it went in.

I want to read you section 4.4. For a first concern, the student may complete a supervised reassessment. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the original and nothing is placed in his record. This is a first concern.

I can read 4.4 myself, Hale. A reassessment for what, and on what evidence, because if Owen sits a rewrite before anyone has shown me anything, that looks like an admission. What do you actually have?
I'll commit to that in writing tonight: nothing goes on his record.
I'm writing that down: in writing tonight, nothing on his record. That's 4.4, and it's the least you owe him. It still doesn't tell me why there's a zero at all, so what do you have, Hale?
So will you agree to the rewrite?
No. Not until I've seen something a person can check, with a date on it, that ties this to Owen's essay. Until then, the zero comes off.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

In today's meeting you acknowledged that the zero was entered before I was contacted, contrary to procedure 4.2, and you committed under procedure 4.4 that nothing will be placed on Owen's record. I still require the zero to be withdrawn, since you have shown me no evidence that a person can check. I expect your written confirmation tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Fallback position; she got your commitment to confirm in writing tonight that nothing goes on Owen's record, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and wants to see dated evidence she can check before agreeing to anything else. The fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you didn't reach it because you never put any evidence on the table.
What moved her: You admitted in one sentence that entering the zero before calling home was wrong, then committed in writing to 4.4, which met her fallback demand and took her record fear off the table.
What cost ground: You offered and then pressed the rewrite before showing any evidence, so agreeing would have looked to her like admitting Owen did something.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence never came near that night because you showed none. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after your apology for the 4.2 breach, show her one dated document tied to Owen's own work that she can check herself, and only then bring up the 4.4 reassessment.
